messages.body_plain:
Dear colleagues,

I attach a PhD opportunity on behalf of Antonio Hernández-Matías, from the University of Barcelona. The candidate needs to have a completed BSc. in Biology, Environmental Sciences, Ecology, or a related discipline, plus a master's degree. This opportunity is not funded yet, but the selected candidate will apply for a grant from the Spanish Research Ministry (FPU). A summary follows below, and more information can be found in the attached file.

Raptors under human pressure: agricultural intensification, energy infrastructure and conservation across spatial scales

Birds of prey are sensitive indicators of environmental change, and many
populations face two major pressures: agricultural intensification and the rapid
expansion of energy infrastructure. How do these pressures affect raptor
distribution, abundance and population trends? Do these effects vary across
Catalonia, Spain and Europe? And what do the findings mean for biodiversity
conservation and territorial planning, including decisions on energy development?

This PhD will examine how agricultural intensification and energy infrastructure
shape the distribution, abundance and population trends of raptors at three spatial
scales: Catalonia, Spain and Europe. The research will be developed within
RAPTORCONS, a research project funded by the Spanish State Research Agency
(Agencia Estatal de Investigación, AEI). You will work with large datasets from bird
atlases, long-term monitoring programmes and citizen science platforms, using
advanced statistical approaches to address challenges associated with
observational data, including differences in sampling effort and observation
processes

All the best,

Jaume A. Badia-Boher

Von: National Centre for Statistical Ecology Members Mailing List <NC...@JISCMAIL.AC.UK> im Auftrag von Fergus Chadwick <00010a748c74b4e...@JISCMAIL.AC.UK>

Betreff: PhD Opportunity: Data-driven biology from imperfect observations

Hi All,

I would be grateful if you would share this PhD opportunity with anyone you think might be interested. I think it’s going to be a really cool project with a nice mix of gnarly stats, complicated observation processes, fish and invertebrates!

Full title: Data-driven biology from imperfect observations: integrating professional and citizen-science biodiversity data

FindAPhD Link with full description: https://www.findaphd.com/phds/project/eastbio-data-driven-biology-from-imperfect-observations-integrating-professional-and-citizen-science-biodiversity-data/?p200393

Brief Summary: This CASE PhD, in partnership with WildFish, will develop statistical methods to integrate citizen-science and professional river monitoring data. Using SmartRivers macroinvertebrate observations, the student will quantify sampling, detection and identification errors and develop hierarchical Bayesian models that account for differences in data quality. The project will establish when (or if!) volunteer-collected data can improve regulatory assessments, optimise professional monitoring and quality control, and produce transferable, open-source tools for integrating imperfect biological observations across diverse monitoring programmes.

Funding Summary: This project is part of the EastBio Doctoral Landscape Award (https://biology.ed.ac.uk/eastbio/about-eastbio) and, if the applicant is successful, will be funded at the UKRI rate with a generous research and training grant. The selection process is outlined here: https://biology.ed.ac.uk/eastbio/eastbio-recruitment/selection-process.

Contact: Any questions, please get in touch with me at  fergusj...@st-andrews.ac.uk! Happy to have informal chats about the project prior to submitting an application.

Best wishes,

Fergus J Chadwick (he/him/his)

Lecturer in Statistics

School of Mathematics and Statistics

University of St Andrews

Room 113, The Observatory, University of St Andrews, Scotland KY16 9LZ

I work flexibly and may send emails outside normal working hours. Please only reply when convenient for you to do so.

To unsubscribe from the NCSE list, click the following link:
https://www.jiscmail.ac.uk/cgi-bin/WA-JISC.exe?SUBED1=NCSE&A=1

Dear colleagues,

I would again like to advertise a postdoctoral opportunity on behalf of Prof. Antonio Hernández-Matías, from the University of Barcelona. Please see the attached document.

The opportunity is to apply for a funded position in his lab using the Juan de la Cierva funding programme from the Spanish government. The applicant should have a completed PhD within the last two years.

To express interest or for further information, please contact Antonio directly (email address in the attachment).

Best,

Jaume
